title: VMCS (Virtual Machine Control Structure)
summary: The VMCS is the data structure used by Intel VT-x to control a virtual machine. It contains: guest state (registers, RIP, RSP, CR0-4, etc.), host state (registers to restore on VM exit), VM-execution controls (which events cause VM exits), VM-exit controls (what to save on exit), VM-entry controls (what to load on entry), and VM-exit information (reason, qualification). The VMCS is 4KB, accessed via VMREAD/VMWRITE instructions.

structure.meaning: Guest RIP, RSP, RFLAGS, CR0-4, DR7, segment registers, etc. Loaded on VM entry.
Host RIP, RSP, CR0, CR3, CR4, etc. Loaded on VM exit.
Pin-based (external interrupts, NMI), primary processor-based (HLT, INVLPG, CR access, I/O, MSR, etc.), secondary processor-based (EPT, RDTSCP, VPID, etc.).
Save debug controls, save IA32_PAT, load IA32_PAT, save IA32_EFER, load IA32_EFER, etc.
Load debug controls, IA32_PAT, IA32_EFER, inject event, etc.
Exit reason (16 bits), exit qualification (64 bits), guest linear address, guest physical address, etc.
Guest physical → host physical translation. 4-level page table (like regular paging but for guest physical addresses).

notes: VMCS is used by KVM, Xen, Hyper-V, and VMware for hardware virtualization.
VMREAD/VMWRITE instructions access VMCS fields by encoding (field index).
EPT (Extended Page Tables) provides nested paging (guest physical → host physical).
VPID (Virtual Processor ID) tags TLB entries to avoid flushes on VM switch.
VT-x supports 2-level (VMX root/non-root) and EPT for memory virtualization.
